newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: BWT extends bull run, surges 10 percent.
newsitem.headline: BWT extends bull run, surges 10 percent.

text.p: The spectacular bull run of water-treatment company BWT forged ahead on Thursday with the shares surging nearly 10 percent, taking their gains to 37 percent in the last four weeks.
"Demand is coming from all over the place -- from international and domestic investors," said a trader in Vienna.

At 0902 GMT, BWT stood 150 schillings, or 9.55 percent, higher to record a fresh high for the year at 1,720 schillings. Turnover was vibrant at 22,563 lots. It earlier climbed to 1,738 schillings. Meanwhile, the ATX index of 21 blue chips stood one percent lower.
"Nobody looks at the stock when it doesn't move. But when it's kissed to life, suddenly everyone wants it," said another trader, adding "there's still room to 1,800, maybe even 1,850."

BWT has seen dogged demand since the company announced in March it was developing a new water-treatment technology that it expected would bring in extra sales of 700 million schillings in the year 2001, and already sales of 200 million and earnings of 56 million next year.
"BWT's a very interesting story. There's been a lot of market rumours on their various technologies and it's got good prospects," said a London-based analyst.

Traders said demand had been further fuelled by the issue of options on BWT's ordinary shares, but that the chunk of buying was "real investor demand". -- Julia Ferguson, Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12 256
